doc.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Portrait of Sheila and jingle work
title: Recording Portrait of Sheila at Van Gelder's; Denzil Best
summary: On her first record under her name, engineer Rudy Van Gelder is strict and Denzil Best tells Russell she scares him because he never knows if she will make it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well, let‟s talk about this session. Let‟s talk about the portrait of, of Sheila, because this is your first one under your name.
Um… I don‟t know if you want to talk about, uh, critical reception, but I‟m interested in, you know, this guitar, bass, drums, plus it‟s got Denzil Best on it, too…
You know, with… Miles got credit for writing [inaudible].
So, and both Ken and I are drummers. And of course, George Russell was a drummer until…

…and fired George. So, so, can we talk a little bit about this session? And if you could tell the, um, you know, for the historical record, something about Denzil Best „cause, you know, unfortunately, he‟s [inaudible].

Well, the one thing that we, we recorded this at, at, um, Rudy Van Gelder‟s. And Rudy was tough. You know, he was very careful. I remember we had a break, and uh, Swallow and I started going up the steps to go to the… we thought the bathroom was… “Where are you going?” He flipped out, you know. And we said, “Oh, well, we thought the bathroom was…” “No, it‟s not. It‟s down here.” [laughs] I said, “Oh, okay.” But I remembered that. But uh, I was in a booth and, uh, Denzil was… You know what Denzil said? [laughs] What he said to George? He said, “She scares me.” [laughs] “I never know if she‟s gonna make it.” [laughs] Oh, God. And when George told me that later, I said, “Oh,” you know, I was kinda like hurt. I took it as kind of an insult. But years later, I said, “No, it was…” I probably… I didn‟t think I was out. I never thought I was out, you know. But obviously, Denzil got scared in a funny sense, you know. I‟m sure nothing would scare Denzil Best. [laughs] But he was very sweet to work with, very… Brown, C.: „Cause you were so deep, Sheila.
Oh, I don‟t know. Brown, C.: [imitating]
I don‟t know what it was. I have no clue. Brown, C.: That‟s what it was.
